examples.ko: 어머니를 위해 일하는 아이의 마음이 갸륵해요.
examples.en: The child's heart in working for his mother is touching.

examples.ko: 어려운데도 이웃을 돕다니 참 갸륵한 사람이에요.
examples.en: Helping neighbors even in hard times, what an admirable person.

examples.ko: 동생을 돌보는 그 마음씨가 갸륵하게 느껴졌어요.
examples.en: Her kindness in looking after her little brother felt admirable.
I was often praised for how admirable my devotion was.

examples.ko: 매일 아침 할아버지께 인사하는 모습이 갸륵하네요.
examples.en: The way you greet your grandfather every morning is lovely.

examples.ko: 그 아이의 효심이 하도 갸륵해서 모두 칭찬했어요.
examples.en: The child's filial devotion was so admirable that everyone praised it.

explain: 주로 어린 사람이나 아랫사람의 착하고 기특한 마음씨나 정성을 보고 어른이 감탄할 때 써요. 윗사람에게 쓰면 실례가 될 수 있어요. 말투가 조금 예스러워서 대화보다 글에서 더 자주 보여요.
explain_en: Elders mainly use it when moved by the kind heart or devotion of a young or junior person. It can sound rude if used about someone senior. The tone is somewhat old-fashioned, so it appears more in writing than in conversation.

examples.ko: 어린 시절 우리 집은 형편이 곤궁했어요.
examples.en: My family was hard up when I was a child.

examples.ko: 곤궁한 살림에도 부모님은 저를 학교에 보내셨어요.
examples.en: Even in their poor circumstances, my parents sent me to school.
Life became hard after the business failed.

examples.ko: 곤궁할 때 도와준 사람을 평생 잊지 못해요.
examples.en: I can never forget the person who helped me when I was in need.

examples.ko: 그는 곤궁하게 살면서도 늘 남을 도왔어요.
examples.en: Even while living in poverty, he always helped others.

examples.ko: 지금은 곤궁하지만 곧 나아질 거라고 믿어요.
examples.en: Things are tough now, but I believe they'll get better soon.

explain: '가난하다'보다 격식 있고 글에 어울리는 말이에요. 돈이 없어서 살기 힘든 형편을 말하고 보통 '형편, 살림, 생활이 곤궁하다'로 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '어렵다', '형편이 안 좋다'라고 많이 말해요.
explain_en: It is more formal and written-sounding than '가난하다'. It describes being in hard circumstances for lack of money, usually in '형편/살림/생활이 곤궁하다'. In daily conversation people more often say '어렵다' or '형편이 안 좋다'.

examples.en: The hem of these long-worn pants is fraying and hanging loose.
The sole of my shoe is flapping loose, so I need to buy new ones.
The torn cloth fluttered in tatters in the wind.
I have to fix the dangling, frayed bag strap.
The sleeve was in tatters, but I wore it out anyway.
The paper stuck on the wall is hanging in shreds.

explain: 찢어지거나 해진 것이 늘어져서 흔들리는 모습에 써요. '너덜대다'도 같은 뜻으로 쓰고, '너덜너덜'과 같은 말뿌리에서 나온 짝말이에요.
explain_en: It describes something torn or worn that hangs down and swings. '너덜대다' means the same, and it is a companion word to '너덜너덜'.

examples.ko: 파일 변환은 몇 초밖에 안 걸려요.
examples.en: Converting a file takes only a few seconds.

examples.ko: 이 앱에서 사진 형식 변환이 가능해요.
examples.en: You can convert photo formats in this app.

examples.ko: 단위 변환 표를 보고 마일을 킬로미터로 바꿨어요.
examples.en: I used a unit conversion table to change miles into kilometers.
An error occurred during the document conversion.

examples.ko: 에너지 변환 효율이 높은 기계를 개발했어요.
examples.en: They developed a machine with high energy conversion efficiency.

examples.ko: 한 번의 변환으로 모든 파일의 형식이 맞춰져요.
examples.en: One conversion makes all the files the same format.

explain: 보통 '파일 변환', '단위 변환', '에너지 변환'처럼 앞에 말이 붙어서 써요. '변화'는 저절로 달라지는 것이고, 변환은 형식이나 모양을 다른 것으로 일부러 바꾸는 일이에요.
explain_en: It usually comes after another word, as in '파일 변환' (file conversion), '단위 변환' (unit conversion) and '에너지 변환' (energy conversion). '변화' is change that happens on its own, while 변환 is deliberately turning the form of something into another form.

examples.en: On weekends the market is bustling with people.

examples.ko: 좁은 방에서 여섯 식구가 복닥거리며 살았어요.
examples.en: Six family members lived crammed together in a small room.
Every morning the subway station is crowded with commuters.
I woke up to the sound of the kids bustling about.
It was a holiday, so the whole family was bustling around in the kitchen.
The airport will be very crowded over the holidays.

explain: 사람이 많이 모여 어수선하게 움직이는 모습이에요. 일상에서는 '북적거리다'도 자주 쓰고, '복닥거리다'는 좁은 곳에 모여 있는 느낌이 있어요. 주로 장소나 사람이 주어예요.
explain_en: It describes many people gathering and moving around in a busy, cluttered way. In daily talk '북적거리다' is also common, and '복닥거리다' suggests a cramped space. The subject is usually a place or people.

examples.en: The child is writing in crooked letters.

examples.ko: 줄을 비뚤비뚤 서지 말고 똑바로 서 주세요.
examples.en: Please stand straight instead of in a wobbly line.
Even though the line was drawn crookedly, it's cute.

examples.ko: 길이 비뚤비뚤 나 있어서 운전하기 힘들어요.
examples.en: The road winds crookedly, so it's hard to drive.
It was my first time on a bike, so I rode in a wobbly way.

examples.ko: 케이크 위에 초를 비뚤비뚤 꽂아 놓았어요.
examples.en: I stuck the candles crookedly into the cake.

explain: 글씨, 선, 줄처럼 곧아야 할 것이 고르지 않게 휘거나 기울어 있을 때 써요. '삐뚤삐뚤'은 더 센 느낌의 말이에요. '쓰다, 그리다, 서다, 가다' 같은 동사 앞에 자주 와요.
explain_en: It is used when something that should be straight, like handwriting, a line or a queue, is uneven and bent or tilted. '삐뚤삐뚤' is the stronger-sounding version. It often comes before verbs like '쓰다', '그리다', '서다' and '가다'.

examples.en: My younger sibling runs around outside all day.
Where do you keep running around every weekend?
The child scampers around the house.
I ran around all day, so I'm tired.

examples.ko: 그렇게 빨빨거리지 말고 좀 앉아 있어요.
examples.en: Stop running around like that and sit down for a bit.
The child who was scampering about suddenly got quiet.

explain: 가만히 있지 않고 부지런히 여기저기 돌아다니는 모습에 써요. 말투가 편하고 구어적이라서 격식을 차린 글에는 잘 안 맞아요. 활발한 아이나 바쁘게 다니는 사람을 말할 때 자주 어울려요.
explain_en: It describes someone who can't sit still and keeps going busily from place to place. The tone is casual and spoken, so it doesn't fit formal writing. It suits lively kids or people who are always on the move.

examples.ko: 이 광고 문구는 너무 상투적이라서 기억에 안 남아요.
examples.en: This ad slogan is so clichéd that it doesn't stick in my mind.

examples.ko: 상투적인 인사말은 마음에 잘 와닿지 않아요.
examples.en: Stock greetings don't really touch my heart.

examples.ko: 그 영화는 이야기가 상투적이지 않아서 좋았어요.
examples.en: I liked that movie because the story wasn't formulaic.
He always just says 'Keep up the good work' out of habit.

examples.ko: 편지가 상투적일 수도 있지만 진심은 담겨 있어요.
examples.en: The letter may be conventional, but it carries sincerity.
The ending was clichéd, but the acting was good, so it was fun.

explain: '뻔하다', '진부하다'와 비슷하지만 말이나 표현, 이야기 전개가 늘 하던 대로라는 느낌이 강해요. 대부분 좋지 않은 평가로 쓰여요. '상투적인 표현'처럼 명사 앞에 오거나 '상투적이다'로 써요.
explain_en: It is close to '뻔하다' or '진부하다', but stresses that an expression or plot is just the usual stock version. It is mostly a negative judgment. You can use it before a noun, as in '상투적인 표현', or as '상투적이다'.

examples.en: As the current saying goes, kids these days live a 'god-tier life'.

examples.ko: 시쳇말이 너무 많아서 이해가 안 돼요.
examples.en: There is so much trendy slang that I don't understand it.
Trendy slang goes out of fashion quickly.

examples.ko: 교수님이 수업에서 시쳇말을 써서 웃음이 터졌어요.
examples.en: The professor used trendy slang in class and everyone burst out laughing.
It would be fun to make a dictionary of trendy slang.

examples.ko: 시쳇말에 약한 아버지는 늘 뜻을 물어보세요.
examples.en: My father is weak on trendy slang and always asks what it means.

explain: '시쳇말로'의 꼴로 가장 많이 써요. 이야기 중간에 요즘 표현을 끌어와 '요즘 말로 하면'처럼 덧붙일 때 쓰는 말이에요. 일상 대화에서는 '요즘 말로'가 더 흔하고, 시쳇말은 글이나 방송에서 자주 보여요. 비슷한 말로 '유행어'가 있어요.
explain_en: It is most often used as '시쳇말로', to bring in a current expression in the middle of a story, like 'in today's words'. In daily talk '요즘 말로' is more common, and 시쳇말 shows up more in writing and broadcasts. A similar word is '유행어'.

examples.en: The little children are walking after their mother in a row.
The small flowerpots in the yard sit together nicely.
The ducklings walked in a little line, close together.
My little siblings, who were all small together, have already grown up.
The market is full of small shops that look snugly packed together.
As the word says, the islands were small and numerous.

explain: 작고 고만고만한 것들이 많이 모여 있을 때 써요. 보통 '올망졸망한 아이들'처럼 사람이나 작은 물건 앞에서 꾸며 줘요.
explain_en: It is used when many small, similar things are gathered together. It usually modifies people or small objects, as in '올망졸망한 아이들' (a bunch of little kids).

en: leave a will; say one's dying wishes

examples.en: Before passing away, my grandfather left his last words to the family.
He stated in his will that his property should be shared among his children.
The king left his last words, entrusting the country to his son.
Do you have any last words to leave?

examples.ko: 그분이 어떤 내용을 유언했는지 아무도 몰라요.
examples.en: Nobody knows what he said as his last wishes.

examples.ko: 할머니는 병원에서 조용히 유언하고 눈을 감으셨어요.
examples.en: My grandmother quietly left her last words in the hospital and passed away.

explain: 죽기 전에 남기는 말이나 뜻을 남길 때 써요. 일상에서는 '유언을 남기다'나 '유언을 하다'가 훨씬 자연스럽고, '유언하다'는 글이나 이야기에서 더 자주 보여요. 높일 때는 '유언하시다'예요.
explain_en: It is used for leaving words or wishes before death. In everyday speech '유언을 남기다' or '유언을 하다' sounds more natural, while 유언하다 appears more in writing and stories. The honorific form is 유언하시다.

examples.en: A philanthropist donated books to the school.

examples.ko: 그분은 조용히 돕는 자선가로 알려져 있어요.
examples.en: He is known as a quiet philanthropist.
Philanthropists gathered and raised a fund.
I want to become a philanthropist someday too.
With a benefactor's help, the children received scholarships.
I met a famous philanthropist and listened to his story.

explain: 돈이나 재능으로 어려운 사람을 꾸준히 돕는 사람에게 써요. 비슷한 말로 '기부자'는 한 번 낸 사람도 포함하고, '독지가'는 더 격식 있는 말이에요.
explain_en: It is used for people who steadily help those in need with money or talent. '기부자' (donor) can include someone who gave just once, and '독지가' is a more formal word.

examples.ko: 문장 끝에 줄임표를 찍으면 말을 다 안 한 느낌이 나요.
examples.en: If you put an ellipsis at the end of a sentence, it feels like you left something unsaid.
If there are too many ellipses, the writing feels awkward.
You sent only an ellipsis in the message, so I was worried.
Ellipses also appear often in the dialogue of novels.
The writer expressed a hesitant feeling with an ellipsis.
What words might come after the ellipsis?

explain: '마침표', '쉼표'처럼 문장 부호 이름이에요. 말을 줄였거나 망설이는 느낌을 줄 때 써요. 메시지에서는 '점점점'이라고 말하기도 해요.
explain_en: Like '마침표' and '쉼표', it is the name of a punctuation mark. It suggests words left out or hesitation. In text messages people sometimes call it '점점점' (dot dot dot).

examples.en: Write dialogue inside double quotation marks.
How are double and single quotation marks different?
We use double quotation marks for direct quotes.

examples.ko: 문장 끝에 큰따옴표를 닫는 걸 잊었어요.
examples.en: I forgot to close the double quotation mark at the end of the sentence.
How do you type a double quotation mark on the keyboard?

examples.ko: 큰따옴표 안에 작은따옴표를 쓸 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can put single quotation marks inside double quotation marks.

explain: 사람의 말이나 글을 그대로 옮길 때 쓰는 "" 부호예요. 속으로 한 생각이나 강조할 때는 보통 작은따옴표 ''를 써요. 말할 때는 '쌍따옴표'라고도 해요.
explain_en: This is the "" mark used to reproduce someone's spoken or written words exactly. For inner thoughts or emphasis, the single quotation mark '' is usually used. In speech, people also say '쌍따옴표'.
